title: controlplane-seed-module-terraform-idempotent-initializer
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (controlplane-seed) that performs deterministic, idempotent initialization of Redwood Private EKS control planes. The module will focus on the minimal, verifiable set of resources required to bring a control plane to a healthy, observable state in a VPC-based private deployment, and expose upgrade-safe hooks and health probes for automated lifecycle orchestration.
background: Current private EKS provisioning flows are composed of multiple ad-hoc Terraform modules and imperative scripts. We've seen flakes during upgrades and race conditions when control-plane components are partially initialized. Operators need a compact, well-documented initializer that is safe to apply repeatedly, emits structured health status, and supports incremental upgrades without destructive mutations.
goals: Provide a single Terraform module that produces a consistent minimal control-plane skeleton (IAM roles, nodegroup bootstrap config, control-plane security groups, required SSM/SSO parameters).
Embed preflight validations and post-apply health checks that return structured status (ok/warning/error) suitable for automation pipelines.
Include non-destructive upgrade hooks (resource version locks, benign drift detection) and quick rollback markers for failed upgrades.
Ship documentation and an integration test harness that runs in CI against a disposable account to validate idempotency and upgrade scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Module can be applied repeatedly on the same workspace/id without creating duplicate resources or throwing unexpected lifecycle diffs.
Module provides a documented output 'seed_health' with one of: OK, DEGRADED, FAILED and a human-readable reason string.
Automated CI job runs the module create -> apply changes -> apply again (no-op) -> simulate upgrade -> rollback, and all steps pass in the test harness.
Module exposes a 'safety_mode' toggle (strict|permissive) and in strict mode refuses destructive updates that could delete control-plane-critical resources.
Integration docs + an example Terragrunt wrapper are added under docs/priv-controlplane/seed-module.md and linked from the README.
technical_notes: Use Terraform 1.6+ features: resource 'for_each' with stable keys and 'prevent_destroy' lifecycle where appropriate.
Minimize provider-level mutations during upgrades by separating mutable metadata from identity resources (e.g., create IAM roles in a dedicated submodule with stable naming).
Health checks: implement a lightweight AWS-native probe pattern (EC2 metadata, ELB target health, EKS control-plane API status checks) and aggregate into a single output variable.
Expose 'preflight_checks' as an optional list of boolean expressions so callers can opt into advanced verifications (KMS key access, route table attachments, DNS delegation).
Design module inputs to be explicit (no reliance on implicit data lookup) to make idempotency easier across accounts and CI runs.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Choosing stricter defaults reduces operator error but increases friction for teams with legacy setups — mitigated by the 'safety_mode' toggle.
Relying on cloud-native health checks keeps runtime dependencies small but may miss app-level regressions; we'll complement with Redwood Console synthetic checks later.
Complexity of idempotency increases module size and test surface; we limit scope to control-plane essentials only.
implementation_plan: 1) Create module scaffold with clear inputs/outputs and submodules (identity, networking, controlplane-config). 2) Add preflight and post-apply health probe implementation with a simple JSON health output. 3) Implement safety_mode and prevent_destroy policies. 4) Add Terratest/infra test harness for create/apply/reapply/upgrade/rollback scenarios. 5) Author docs and example Terragrunt wrapper. 6) Run pilot with one internal customer and iterate.
rollout_plan: Start as opt-in: publish module in private registry, onboard one infra team for pilot. Collect metrics from CI runs (idempotency failures), and after 2 successful pilots, recommend as the default initializer for new Private control plane clusters. Integrate module outputs into provisioning state machine for automated health gating.
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate + tflint on module code
Integration: CI job that provisions disposable infra in sandbox account, runs full idempotency and upgrade matrix
Chaos: CI scenario that simulates transient API failures and validates rollback markers are durable
Security: run custom static analysis on IAM policies to verify least-privilege and add a gated manual review for high-privilege roles
dependencies: ENG-121314 (eks-controlplane-prober) - for reusing existing control-plane API probes
Infra Tooling - approval to create disposable sandbox accounts for CI
Docs - space in priv-controlplane docs for example Terragrunt wrapper
